newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran launches first official Arabic daily.
newsitem.headline: Iran launches first official Arabic daily.

text.p: Iran, whose official language is Persian, on Saturday published its first Arabic newspaper "al-Wefaq" in its bid to forge friendship between the Islamic republic and Arab states.
"Al-Wefaq is an Arabic publication for Iran and an Iranian publication for the Arabs," al-Wefaq, published by the state-run IRNA news agency said in its first issue.
The London-based Asharq al-Awsat said on Saturday that more than 20 Arab journalists would contribute to the new publication.

"Iran and the Arab world enjoy a rich cultural and religious heritage and have tremendous potential to build on long-standing friendships between them," the English-language Iran Daily said in an editorial welcoming the new daily.
Diplomats said al-Wefaq comes at a time when Iran is moving closer toward reconciling strained ties with neighbouring oil-rich Gulf Arab states.
